steps.sent: Why did it fall so much?
steps.answer:
The portfolio’s worst drop ran from February 18, 2025 to August 1, 2025. It fell from $1,747 to $963, a dollar decline of $784, or 44.9%.

The run itself cannot identify one exact cause. It shows a buy-and-hold position in a single stock, with one purchase and no sales, so the portfolio had no built-in way to reduce exposure during the decline. The strategy also had 68.6% annualized volatility, which is consistent with a large move in either direction.

The timing overlaps with several documented pressures. On April 3, broad technology stocks sold off sharply after new U.S. tariffs raised fears of a trade war and recession, as Reuters reported in its coverage of the market rout. That likely added market pressure to a growth-oriented cloud stock such as DOCN. Company-specific concerns were also reported in July, including DOCN’s 98.2% first-quarter net revenue retention and relatively low gross margin, in this July analysis of the stock.

This was not simply a period of consistently worsening company news. DigitalOcean’s first-quarter results release reported revenue growth and continued profitability. Its second-quarter results and raised full-year guidance were released on August 5, after the run’s recorded bottom on August 1, so they cannot explain the decline inside the measured window. The clearest explanation is therefore a combination of concentrated single-stock exposure, high volatility, broad technology-market selling, and investor concerns about DOCN’s customer retention and infrastructure costs, rather than one event proven by the backtest.
